title: Why HashMap is not thread-safe

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: HashMap has no locking. Two threads that put at the same time can corrupt its internal structure: one write can overwrite another, the size counter can be wrong, and a resize can lose entries. Reads during a write can see half-updated state, and iteration can throw ConcurrentModificationException. Use ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent use, or wrap access in one lock with Collections.synchronizedMap.

points.title: Lost updates
points.why: Two concurrent puts can overwrite each other or corrupt the bucket structure.

points.title: Right alternative
points.why: ConcurrentHashMap is built for concurrent access and is the usual answer.
